title: Top 5 Common BIM Workflow Mistakes and Their Solution {{year}}
summary: Discover common BIM workflow mistakes and how to avoid them. Learn how teams can build better workflows and efficiently complete AEC projects.
body_text: Why Do BIM Workflows Break Down? BIM workflows disintegrate when the technology and the people using it do not align. So, while BIM enables seamless coordination , here are the most common reasons why it can fail: Lack of BIM Standards: In the absence of accurate modelling standards, naming conventions, and documentation protocols, every team may follow a different approach. This often leads to confusion, chaos, and patchy coordination across the project lifecycle. Poor Collaboration: BIM relies on architects, engineers, contractors, and consultants working together. Delayed communication, isolated workflows, or limited data sharing can cause design conflicts and project delays. Incorrect Models: When teams do not update the central model regularly, others may continue working with outdated information. This raises the likelihood of errors and discrepancies during construction. Limited BIM Skills: BIM software is only as effective as the professionals using it. Insufficient training or a lack of understanding of BIM processes can lead to inaccurate modelling, weak workflows, and missed project requirements. Resistance to Process Changes: Implementing BIM coordination requires organisations to change long-established workflows. When teams continue following traditional methods instead of adopting collaborative BIM practices , the workflow becomes fragmented and loses efficiency. What Are the 5 Most Common BIM Workflow Mistakes? Even with the right BIM software stack and skilled professionals, AEC projects can experience workflow issues. Let’s explore the 5 most common BIM workflow mistakes and how to dodge them: Mistake Impact How to Avoid Underutilizing BIM Limits BIM to 3D modelling, reducing collaboration, coordination, and project insights. Use BIM across design, coordination, documentation, and project management. Poor Quality Modelling Creates inaccurate models, leading to coordination issues and costly rework. Follow BIM standards, conduct regular model reviews, and maintain data accuracy. Inconsistent Data Management Causes outdated information, duplicate files, and version conflicts. Use a Common Data Environment (CDE) with standardised naming and version control. Irregular Communication Delays decision-making and increases the risk of design conflicts. Hold regular coordination meetings and share model updates consistently. Integration with Other Workflows such as 4D BIM and 5D BIM Results in manual work, disconnected data, and reduced project efficiency. Integrate BIM with scheduling, costing, and project management tools. How Do Standards and Collaboration Prevent Costly Errors? BIM projects rely on multiple teams working on the same project data throughout the design and construction lifecycle. This applies using proper software, BIM standards , and BIM collaboration processes that help avoid expensive rework. Here’s how this can be achieved: Uniform Modelling Methods: Setting a project-wide modelling protocol for object parameters, detailing, and documentation ensures that every team member creates and interprets models in the same way. Aligning these standards with frameworks such as ISO 19650 improves model quality and abates coordination mistakes. Common Data Environment (CDE): A Common Data Environment such as Autodesk Cloud Collaboration provides a central location where project information, models, drawings, and documents are stored. Using a single point of information helps teams avoid duplicate files, outdated information, and version conflicts. Regular Coordination Meetings: Frequent coordination sessions allow project stakeholders to review project progress and resolve issues before they affect downstream activities. This keeps the entire team in sync throughout the BIM workflow. Clash Detection: Routine BIM model coordination helps identify conflicts between architectural, structural, and MEP systems before construction starts. Resolving these issues reduces rework, delays, and unexpected project costs. Defined Roles: Assigning responsibilities for model creation, review, and approvals ensures accountability across the project team. When everyone understands their job, information flows more efficiently, and collaboration becomes more effective. Which Tools Help Improve BIM Workflow Efficiency? BIM modelling software offers a dashboard where professionals can view, modify, and manage project components. They also help in enhancing construction documentation and keep project information consistent across teams. Let’s explore the key BIM tools that enhance operational efficiency: Revit: It is one of the most widely used BIM authoring tools for architectural, structural, and MEP modelling. Revit software can generate coordinated drawings, schedules, and quantities from a unified model and maintain precise project documentation. Navisworks: It enables teams to combine discipline-specific models for coordination, clash detection, and construction simulation. Identifying design conflicts before construction helps minimise rework and project delays. Revizto: Revizto streamlines BIM coordination by bringing drawings and issue tracking onto a collaborative platform. It allows project teams to assign tasks, monitor progress, and resolve design conflicts more efficiently. Autodesk Forma: This software supports conceptual and schematic phases of architecture and urban design projects. Its key features include site analysis, study of environmental factors, and building performance. Autodesk Model Checker: Conceived on Forge, a cloud-based developer platform, this tool automates BIM model validation. It allows professionals to check BIM files against predefined standards and project requirements to streamline BIM workflow. Solibri: Solibri is a quality assurance tool that validates BIM models for rule compliance, data accuracy, and coordination issues. It enables project teams to identify errors early and improve the reliability of project information. Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC): ACC provides a cloud-based CDE where teams can store and manage project information. It improves collaboration by ensuring all stakeholders always work on the latest project data. How Can Teams Build Better BIM Workflows? Building a practical BIM workflow depends on set processes, project coordination standards, and clear communication. Below are the key measures that can aid professionals in creating their workflow: Define Project Guidelines: Establish modelling standards, file structures, and documentation protocols before commencing the project. A uniform approach helps teams work with clarity of thought and achieve timely milestones. Assign Responsibilities: Every stakeholder should understand their scope, deliverables, and timelines. Explaining responsibilities for architects, engineers, contractors, and BIM managers improves accountability and prevents duplication of work. Use a Common Data Environment: An integrated platform ensures all project information and documents can be accessed from one location. This confirms every team member works with the latest project data and reduces version control issues. Host Coordination Reviews: Schedule coordination meetings to review models, discuss design changes, and resolve clashes. Frequent reviews help identify issues early and keep the project aligned with its objectives. Leverage BIM Collaboration Tools: Software such as Autodesk Construction Cloud, Revizto, and Navisworks streamlines model sharing, clash detection, issue tracking, and communication between disciplines. These tools improve coordination and support informed decision-making. Invest in Continuous BIM Training: BIM workflows continue to evolve alongside new software capabilities and industry standards. Regular upskilling helps teams stay competent and follow best practices, adopt efficient workflows, and make better use of BIM technologies. Enrolling in a comprehensive BIM training such as Novatr’s BIM Professional Program can also enhance workflows and offer practical tips for real-world projects.

title: AtriCure Announces the First Patients Treated with Novel Dual Energy Platform
summary: New technology combines Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) and Advanced Radiofrequency Ablation with AtriCure’s EnCompass® clamp to reduce treatment time for surgical ablation patientsMASON, Ohio--Dec. 11, 2025-- AtriCure, Inc. (Nasdaq: ATRC), a leading innovator in surgical treatments and therapies for atrial fibrillation (Afib), left atrial appendage (LAA) management and post-operative pain management, today announced successful first-in-human treatments using its novel dual energy platform that integrates Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) with Advanced Radiofrequency Ablation (Advanced RFA). The procedures were performed by Dr. Adrian Pick in collaboration with the site Principal Investigator Professor Jayme Bennetts, at Victorian Heart Hospital in Australia under approval from the Monash Health Human Research Ethics Committee (HREC).The new platform delivers the benefits of both technologies—combining the proven safety and effectiveness of radiofrequency (RF) ablation with the efficiency of PFA. Advanced RFA reduces ablation time significantly, while PFA enables transmural ablation in seconds. In the first two patients treated, total procedural ablation time to create a box lesion simultaneously isolating the pulmonary veins and the left atrial posterior wall was less than 60 seconds. Each ablation was also tested to prove acute electrical isolation.“For 25 years, we’ve been the leader in cardiac surgical ablation,” said Michael Carrel, President and CEO of AtriCure. “Our innovative EnCompass clamp technology was a significant step in streamlining cardiac surgery ablation procedures. Now, building on the proven performance of our EnCompass clamp, this platform offers the best of both worlds. By pairing Advanced RFA with PFA, we’re delivering unprecedented speed and flexibility for surgeons.”The AtriCure Isolator® Synergy™ ablation system has a long history of safety and clinical effectiveness, supported by extensive published data, including over 100 publications, and has been used to treat over 450,000 patients in the last 20 years. AtriCure began development of the dual energy platform with the goals of shortening RF ablation times and introducing PFA as a complementary energy source. The system allows surgeons to use either modality independently or in combination.“This technology builds on AtriCure’s strong legacy in cardiac surgical ablation,” said Dr. Pick. “Reduced procedure times and trusted devices mean more patients can benefit, and combining the benefits of RF with PFA should further ensure durable results.”The Advanced RFA and PFA technologies are not yet approved for use in any market. AtriCure expects to initiate a clinical trial in the coming year, marking a key milestone in its product development pipeline.About AtriCureAtriCure, Inc. provides innovative technologies for the treatment of Afib and related conditions. Afib affects more than 59 million people worldwide. Surgeons around the globe use AtriCure technologies for the treatment of Afib, reduction of Afib related complications, and post-operative pain management. AtriCure’s Isolator® Synergy™ Ablation System is the first medical device to receive FDA approval for the treatment of persistent and long-standing persistent Afib. AtriCure’s AtriClip® Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion System products are the most widely sold LAA management devices worldwide. AtriCure’s Hybrid AF™ Therapy is a minimally invasive procedure that provides a lasting solution for long-standing persistent Afib patients. AtriCure’s cryoICE cryoSPHERE® and cryoXT® probes are cleared for temporary ablation of peripheral nerves to block pain, providing pain relief in cardiac, thoracic and amputation procedures. title: Perspectives in Aseptic Manufacturing: Start Packaging Development Early: De‑Risk Before You Build
summary: Early collaboration on primary packaging, OEM line design and EU GMP Annex 1 readiness can reduce fill-finish delays and support scalable aseptic manufacturing.
body_text: Eric Kurtz Manager Technical Product Development, BS Chemical Engineering, MBA July 15, 2026 Perspectives in Aseptic Manufacturing: Start Packaging Development Early: De‑Risk Before You Build In aseptic manufacturing, timing is a strategic advantage. Packaging development should not follow fill/finish line selection. It should inform it. Early Collaboration Early collaboration between container suppliers, original equipment manufacturer (OEM) partners, and drug developers helps ensure that primary packaging components can be successfully handled, filled, and processed on the intended equipment. Engaging during the component development phase allows teams to understand requirements for format parts, transport mechanisms, pump technologies, plunger placement, and in‑process controls before equipment fabrication begins. These decisions influence more than line layout. They affect dosing accuracy, inert gas integration, automation capability, and long‑term flexibility. Retrofitting a filling line after the fact in order to accommodate a different syringe platform or to enable 100% in‑process weight checks (IPC) can introduce avoidable delays at critical development milestones. Regulatory Expectations Regulatory expectations based on the EU GMP Annex 1 benchmark have reset and further reinforced the value of early alignment. Ready‑to‑use component formats, isolator integration, automated introduction technologies, and contamination control strategies must work together as a system. Addressing these variables late in development limits options and increases risk. It is also important to look beyond clinical supply. Will your selected container closure components scale to commercial volumes? Can the same line process additional formats such as vials, syringes, or cartridges with defined format part changeover? Are you building flexibility into your long‑term manufacturing footprint? By mapping packaging strategy to manufacturing strategy early, teams preserve choice and reduce downstream disruption. West collaborates with drug developers and OEM partners from the concept stage through commercialization. By aligning packaging systems with equipment capability and regulatory expectations early, we help reduce risk and accelerate readiness for your next milestone. If you are defining your fill/finish strategy, this is the moment to align packaging development with your future manufacturing goals. For support with selection of packaging components for your fill finish line, Contact Us. title: DeFi Dev Corp. Announces Strategic Leadership Transition of DisclaimerCoin (DONT) to Dedicated Ecosystem Team
summary: BOCA RATON, FL, July 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- DeFi Development Corp. (Nasdaq: DFDV) (the “Company”), the first U.S. public company with a treasury...
body_text: BOCA RATON, FL, July 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- DeFi Development Corp. (Nasdaq: DFDV) (the “Company”), the first U.S. public company with a treasury strategy built to accumulate and compound Solana (“SOL”), today announced the strategic transition of leadership for DisclaimerCoin (“DONT”), the world’s first publicly traded company-created memecoin, to Daniel Reis-Faria, Chief Executive Officer of Nasdaq-listed ZeroStack Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: ZSTK), and a dedicated team focused exclusively on growing the DisclaimerCoin ecosystem. The transition represents the next phase in DisclaimerCoin’s evolution. While DFDV pioneered the historic launch of DONT in January 2026, the Company believes the project’s long-term success is best served by an independent team dedicated full-time to ecosystem development, community growth, partnerships, liquidity expansion, and new utility. DFDV and ZeroStack are not strangers. In September 2025, the companies announced a strategic relationship focused on accelerating institutional Solana adoption through DFDV’s Treasury Accelerator initiative. That existing relationship gave DFDV confidence that the DisclaimerCoin ecosystem would be entrusted to an experienced team with a demonstrated track record operating at the intersection of public markets and digital assets. Daniel Reis-Faria has extensive experience building blockchain businesses, launching token ecosystems, and leading publicly traded companies operating within the digital asset industry. He will assume responsibility for DisclaimerCoin’s continued development, including ecosystem partnerships, liquidity initiatives, community expansion, integrations, and additional utility designed to strengthen the project’s long-term growth. “Launching DisclaimerCoin was never intended to be the finish line,” said Joseph Onorati, Chief Executive Officer of DeFi Development Corp. “It proved that a Nasdaq-listed company could innovate onchain while operating transparently in the public markets. The next chapter requires a team whose sole focus is building the ecosystem every day. Given our existing relationship with Daniel, we believe they are well positioned to take DisclaimerCoin forward.” The announcement follows additional momentum for the DisclaimerCoin ecosystem. Last week, HCMC (Pink Limited Market: HCMC) announced the acquisition of DONT as part of its newly announced digital asset treasury strategy, further expanding institutional awareness surrounding the token. The original vision behind DisclaimerCoin remains unchanged. Created as an experiment exploring the intersection of public markets, internet culture, and onchain communities, the project now enters a new phase under independent leadership focused on accelerating adoption while preserving its unique identity. As part of the transition, the new leadership team will assume governance and stewardship of the remaining DONT originally allocated to the project’s Ecosystem, Growth & Community allocation, providing resources to support ecosystem development, partnerships, liquidity initiatives, community growth, and future expansion. Separately, DFDV will continue to permanently hold its treasury allocation, representing approximately 31.6% of the total $DONT supply , on its balance sheet in accordance with the Company’s original commitment at launch. Following completion of the token transfer, DFDV will no longer serve as the day-to-day steward of the DisclaimerCoin ecosystem. For more information, visit disclaimercoin.com and follow https://x.com/DisclaimerCoin . About DeFi Development Corp. DeFi Development Corp. (Nasdaq: DFDV) has adopted a treasury policy under which the principal holding in its treasury reserve is allocated to SOL. Through this strategy, the Company provides investors with direct economic exposure to SOL, while also actively participating in the growth of the Solana ecosystem. In addition to holding and staking SOL, DeFi Development Corp. operates its own validator infrastructure, generating staking rewards and fees from delegated stake. The Company is also engaged across decentralized finance (DeFi) opportunities and continues to explore innovative ways to support and benefit from Solana’s expanding application layer. The Company is also an AI-powered online platform that connects the commercial real estate industry by providing value-add services and software subscriptions to multifamily and commercial property professionals, as the Company connects the increasingly complex ecosystem that stakeholders have to manage. The Company’s data and software offerings are generally offered on a subscription basis as software as a service. Investor Contact: ir@defidevcorp.com Media Contact: press@defidevcorp.com

title: Les dernières tendances qui façonnent l’industrie manufacturière en 2025
summary: Explorez les tendances de fabrication 2025 avec IA, durabilité et innovation numérique pour surmonter les défis de la chaîne d'approvisionnement et transformer l'industrie.
body_text: Dans un secteur en pleine transformation, l’industrie manufacturière cherche de plus en plus des solutions innovantes pour rester compétitive. En 2025, les chaînes d’approvisionnement sont sous tension et l’incertitude économique freine les investissements, qui restent inférieurs à ceux des années précédentes. Pourtant, c’est dans des conditions difficiles que l’innovation prend tout son sens. Découvrez les enjeux prioritaires pour les dirigeants du secteur et comment ils relèvent ces nouveaux défis. Digitalisation de l’ensemble du secteur Diverses approches d’optimisation numérique sont actuellement mises en œuvre alors que le secteur manufacturier connaît une transformation majeure. De plus en plus d’entreprises intègrent de nouvelles technologies et exploitent des données pour améliorer leurs opérations de production. Le rapport Manufacturing Trends & Technology d’ Aptean indique que 52 % des industriels prévoient d’adopter des technologies émergentes et des solutions basées sur les données en 2025, tandis que 48 % comptent moderniser ou intégrer leurs systèmes existants. Les avancées récentes en matière d’analyse de données permettent aux utilisateurs d’accéder à des informations plus riches et plus pertinentes. Cela favorise une plus grande agilité, l’identification de pistes d’économies et une innovation continue, même en période d’incertitude. S’inspirant du succès de l’industrie automobile dans l’utilisation de solutions technologiques de pointe pour mesurer les performances de flottes de véhicules, le secteur manufacturier prend conscience des avantages liés à la maintenance prédictive et à l’ optimisation des processus . L’essor des logiciels pour usines intelligentes et des capteurs embarqués post-production, désormais plus accessibles et plus fiables, contribue également à réduire les coûts pour les entreprises. Le "grand sujet" : où en sommes-nous avec l’IA ? L’industrie manufacturière est l’un des secteurs les plus fortement impactés par l’intelligence artificielle (IA). De nombreuses industries ont rapidement adopté l’IA, attirées par son potentiel de réduction des coûts et de la charge de travail. L’industrie manufacturière n’a pas fait exception. D’après le Forum économique mondial , 68 % des fabricants, tous secteurs confondus, ont déjà mis en place une forme d’IA dans leurs opérations. Mais l’enthousiasme initial a laissé place à une approche plus stratégique. Selon une étude de Deloitte , les entreprises concentrent désormais leurs efforts sur l’analyse de la contribution réelle de l’IA à leurs objectifs de chiffre d’affaires, à l’amélioration de la productivité et au remplacement des tâches manuelles répétitives. Les organisations se tournent vers l’IA générative pour accélérer leurs processus de fabrication. Comme l’explique un article récent de Forbes , « en exploitant la puissance du design génératif, il devient possible de créer des composants plus solides, plus légers, et utilisant les matériaux de manière plus efficiente. » Dans le domaine de la fabrication additive, « l’impression 3D profite de l’engouement autour de l’IA de nouvelle génération et des outils d’automatisation », affirme François Minec, directeur mondial des polymères 3D chez HP Personalization and 3D Printing, dans le rapport Protolabs 2024 sur les tendances de l’impression 3D . « Les avancées en matière de matériel, de microprogrammes et de logiciels permettent de mettre la data et le suivi des indicateurs clés (KPI) au premier plan, ouvrant la voie à une montée en échelle pour un plus grand nombre d’acteurs. » Chez NASA , le recours à la conception générative collaborative a permis aux ingénieurs d’accélérer significativement le développement de produits. À l’avenir, les entreprises chercheront à identifier les applications de l’IA les plus rentables. Il peut s’agir, par exemple, d’optimiser la conception de pièces, d’automatiser certaines étapes de production ou de réduire les coûts liés à la maintenance prédictive. Comme le résume Forbes : « L’avenir de l’industrie manufacturière ne se résume pas à l’automatisation et à l’IA, mais à la création de systèmes de production plus intelligents, plus durables et plus adaptables. » Faire face à la complexité : renforcer les chaînes d’approvisionnement La gestion des chaînes d’approvisionnement figure parmi les priorités des entreprises innovantes. De plus en plus de fabricants prennent des mesures pour atténuer les risques et protéger leurs chaînes d’approvisionnement contre les vulnérabilités et les coûts liés, par exemple, aux droits de douane. Les organisations adoptent également de nouvelles approches basées sur les données pour guider leurs décisions. Les récentes avancées technologiques incluent la gestion des stocks pilotée par les données, des prévisions plus précises grâce aux données en temps réel et des opportunités d’automatisation. Ces outils permettent aux entreprises d’adapter leur chaîne d’approvisionnement en fonction des conditions du marché. « Les fabricants peuvent s’appuyer sur les données pour s’adapter plus rapidement aux incertitudes qui caractérisent les chaînes d’approvisionnement, et ainsi réduire les interruptions, toujours imprévisibles. L’usage de la blockchain renforce la traçabilité, tandis que les outils en temps réel permettent de garder le contrôle », rapporte ATS . La rapidité et la flexibilité offertes par le modèle de fabrication distribuée par Protolabs représentent une solution idéale pour atténuer les effets des bouleversements économiques et mondiaux. Découvrez comment la relocalisation et la fabrication numérique permettent de naviguer plus sereinement dans un contexte d’approvisionnement instable. Le sujet "vert" : la durabilité À mesure que le changement climatique devient plus pressant, la pression s’intensifie également pour adopter des pratiques de fabrication plus durables. Certains pourraient penser qu’en période de réduction des investissements industriels, les entreprises mettront leurs initiatives durables entre parenthèses, mais ce n’est généralement pas le cas. D’après le rapport 2025 Manufacturing Industry Outlook de Deloitte, les investissements dans la fabrication de technologies propres sont restés solides tout au long de 2024, bien qu’ils aient ralenti par rapport à 2023. Parallèlement, la demande des clients pour des produits à faibles émissions reste stable, et la fabrication écoresponsable continue de répondre à cette exigence. Le seul marché des véhicules électriques devrait atteindre 5 000 milliards de dollars d’ici 2030. Comme le souligne Deloitte , « les clients semblent déterminés à réduire leurs émissions opérationnelles, ce qui devrait continuer à soutenir la demande pour des produits à faibles émissions ». Les entreprises adoptent une approche stratégique de la fabrication durable. Elles explorent, par exemple, l’utilisation de matériaux recyclés , qui présentent des propriétés mécaniques similaires aux matériaux traditionnels. De plus, elles mettent en place des pratiques de production plus sobres, comme la fabrication allégée (lean manufacturing). Le sujet "humanoïde" : collaborer avec les robots et cobots L’industrie manufacturière a été l’un des premiers secteurs à intégrer les robots dans ses opérations quotidiennes. Grâce aux récents progrès en robotique industrielle, ces robots sont aujourd’hui capables de collaborer plus étroitement avec leurs homologues humains. Ils peuvent fonctionner 24 h/24, être configurés pour offrir une grande régularité et éviter certaines erreurs humaines. Bien que leur arrivée ait suscité des inquiétudes concernant le remplacement de la main-d’œuvre humaine, les robots viennent en réalité la compléter. Ils sont dotés de capteurs de pointe et de systèmes de contrôle du mouvement basés sur l’intelligence artificielle. Les robots collaboratifs, appelés aussi « cobots », sont de plus en plus utilisés pour accomplir des tâches répétitives ou dangereuses. Ils permettent de combler les pénuries de main-d’œuvre et contribuent à améliorer la productivité. Le sujet "sensible" : cybersécurité et protection des données Avec la généralisation de la numérisation, la sécurisation et la protection des systèmes de données deviennent plus cruciales que jamais. L’industrie manufacturière cherchera sans doute à renforcer sa gestion des données et sa cybersécurité, surtout avec le recours croissant à l’intelligence artificielle. Selon le Forum économique mondial , l’industrie manufacturière a été l’une des principales cibles de la cybercriminalité ces dernières années, et les menaces persistent. « La transition des systèmes isolés vers des systèmes interconnectés, combinée à l’essor d’internet puis de l’informatique en nuage, a accentué les défis en matière de cybersécurité pour les organisations industrielles. » Le risque cyber devient ainsi systémique, peut se propager rapidement et dépasse souvent la compréhension ou le contrôle d’une seule entité. Face à cela, les entreprises donnent désormais la priorité à la mise en place de pratiques solides en matière de résilience informatique . Et ensuite ? Où va l’industrie ? Lors de sa réunion annuelle de 2025, le Forum économique mondial a comparé le moment que traverse actuellement l’industrie manufacturière à l’arrivée d’internet, une génération plus tôt. Selon ses conclusions, « nous assistons à l’émergence d’un nouveau paradigme industriel où durabilité, intelligence et résilience ne sont plus des priorités concurrentes, mais des forces complémentaires qui se renforcent mutuellement ». Autrement dit, pour faire face aux défis actuels et renforcer leur compétitivité, les industriels misent sur des pratiques numériques plus agiles et innovantes. Cette transition leur permet d’optimiser leurs opérations et de mieux répondre aux enjeux environnementaux. Une approche qui les prépare à un avenir plus durable et plus résilient.

title: Swarmer and Brightline Partner on AI Data Collection and Drone Interoperability for U.S. Department of War
summary: Agreement combines Swarmer’s combat-proven swarm autonomy software with Brightline’s SpatialCore interoperability platform for joint development, technology integration and shared U.S. defense opportunities AUSTIN, Texas, July 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Swarmer, Inc (Nasdaq: SWMR) (“Swarmer” or the “Company”), a drone autonomy software company whose technology has supported more than 100,000 real-world combat missions in Ukraine […]
body_text: Agreement combines Swarmer’s combat-proven swarm autonomy software with Brightline’s SpatialCore interoperability platform for joint development, technology integration and shared U.S. defense opportunities AUSTIN, Texas, July 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Swarmer, Inc (Nasdaq: SWMR) (“Swarmer” or the “Company”), a drone autonomy software company whose technology has supported more than 100,000 real-world combat missions in Ukraine since April 2024, today announced it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Brightline Interactive , a subsidiary of The Glimpse Group. Brightline is a physical AI and spatial computing company that produces SpatialCore, an open standards-based interoperability and operational context platform that enables autonomous systems, AI agents, sensors and digital twins to operate from a shared understanding of the physical world. The agreement covers joint research and development, integration of the two companies’ technologies and the pursuit of shared business opportunities through Brightline’s existing relationships and contracting vehicles with the Department of War. Under the agreement, Swarmer will contribute its autonomy and swarm coordination software, along with years of battle-tested expertise in swarm behavior. Brightline will integrate Swarmer’s technology with SpatialCore to expand access to diverse real-world operational data for AI model training and accelerate model development. Brightline also will provide SpatialCore’s data and communications interoperability layer, support integration of Swarmer’s autonomy software across its ecosystem of connected platforms and programs and leverage its established U.S. defense contracting pathways and customer relationships. “At Swarmer, we believe that the future of warfare will rely on artificial intelligence and the process of training AI models relies heavily on data,” said Alex Fink, President and US CEO of Swarmer. “Combining SpatialCore with Swarmer’s platform could provide access to operational data from virtually any drone, including manufacturers not yet integrated with us. Beyond our own missions, this could unlock data captured during tens of millions of missions flown industry-wide on other platforms that SpatialCore can address, to improve our AI models and iterate faster than ever before.” With more than seven million drones projected to be manufactured worldwide this year, the defining challenge is enabling large numbers of drones to work together autonomously. Artificial intelligence requires large volumes of high-quality operational data to continuously train and improve models. Together, the companies intend to address complementary aspects of that challenge by combining interoperability with autonomous swarm coordination. “Millions of drones are projected to be manufactured every year, and we believe no single company will solve autonomy in isolation,” said Tyler Gates, President and Chief Executive Officer of Brightline Interactive. “Scale only matters if these systems can work together seamlessly, which is the gap SpatialCore closes. Integrating Swarmer’s combat-proven coordination with SpatialCore’s interoperability layer will allow us to give our customers an extended shared operational picture across a much broader set of platforms. This expands both the volume and quality of real-world operational data available to train and improve AI models which will allow us to pursue joint market opportunities together.” About Brightline Interactive Brightline Interactive, a subsidiary of The Glimpse Group (Nasdaq: GGRP), builds SpatialCore, an open standards-based interoperability and operational context platform that enables autonomous systems, AI agents, sensors and digital twins to operate from a shared understanding of the physical world. SpatialCore is built on open data standards backed by NVIDIA, Apple, and the major robotics and simulation platforms. Brightline holds Cooperative Research and Development Agreements with the DOW and is a prime contractor through an OTA with the United States Navy. Brightline is the operating subsidiary of the Glimpse Group (Nasdaq: GGRP). For more information, visit www.brightlineinteractive.com . About Swarmer Swarmer™ (Nasdaq: SWMR) is a defense technology company that specializes in vendor-agnostic software which allows one operator to intuitively control hundreds of autonomous platforms in real time. Swarmer’s primary mission areas include autonomous swarm coordination, integration of multi-domain unmanned systems and AI-powered autonomy software for distributed operations. Swarmer is not a drone manufacturer and does not depend on any single platform, supplier or hardware lifecycle. Instead, Swarmer operates at the intelligence layer, developing autonomy, coordination and decision-making software that enables large numbers of low-cost unmanned systems to operate collectively as one coherent, resilient force. Swarmer’s technology has been rigorously validated in real-world kinetic environments and was first deployed in combat operations in Ukraine in April 2024. Since then, it has completed more than 100,000 combat missions, generating terabytes of proprietary data that informs its machine-learning models and enables the replication of advanced pilot performance at scale. Swarmer’s routine use in combat missions generates continuous streams of telemetry, sensor data and operational feedback which are then used to refine performance, increase resilience and accelerate learning. Swarmer has headquarters in Austin, Texas, and maintains operations and teams in Ukraine, Poland and Estonia. title: Staying connected with customers in the age of big data
summary: The owner of a large supermarket chain approached CGI with how difficult it is to retain customers and attract new ones, especially in their large urban and suburban stores. body_text: The owner of a large supermarket chain approached CGI with how difficult it is to retain customers and attract new ones, especially in their large urban and suburban stores. He felt they were losing sight of their loyal customers and what makes them stay or go. Back when they were a small, local grocer, they knew their customers personally—their likes, dislikes and family members. CGI is now helping this company use big data to regain this knowledge. For example, we use loyalty card data to identify shifts in shopping behavior. Insights are shared through customer-facing channels to prompt cashiers to invite customers into a dialog with a store service representative, assign a call center agent to contact a customer, or adjust mailings accordingly. These are examples of using omni-channel management to create a better customer experience. The retailer is also working with CGI to develop more intelligent ways to identify loyal customers and keep track of them after their initial registration. This includes identifying when loyalty cards are used by unidentified customers, which results in stores losing track of their base and missing opportunities to identify potential new loyal customers. For example, when purchase patterns typical of an elderly woman suddenly changed to beer, chips and video games, it turned out she had given her card to her grandson. The company was able to detect this change and responded by inviting him to receive his own loyalty card. Based on his preferences, they also activated their store app on his mobile phone. The app allows customers to communicate with stores, share shopping experiences and menus with other users, and arrange to meet up for coffee while in the store. The company is taking the app even further by organizing user shopping lists to match the floor plans of their stores, and notifying users of discounts and products they might like, based on past behavior. It all starts with the customers opting in. Conversations with customers begin by explaining the potential benefits of opting in and how the shared information is used. Since this is a sensitive topic, the company has established a data-ethics committee that evaluates all of their big data initiatives, so they don’t cross the line of being “big brother”. None of the information is shared with third parties, as their policy is based on being a trusted advisor. Basically, this very-large enterprise is applying the three key principles they have had since they started their first store so many years ago: Know your customer. Engage in a conversation with customers. Work as a trusted advisor, always safeguarding the information customers share. By using today’s big data technologies, they can apply these principles on a much larger scale to continually improve customer satisfaction and grow sales. In essence, they are bringing back their ability to connect with their customers in a digital world, and on their customers’ terms. CGI is proud to be of service to this company based on our customer intelligence services and in depth experience in customer analytics.

title: ¿Cómo saber cuáles son los productos más vendidos en Mercado Libre?
summary: Descubre las mejores estrategias para identificar los productos más vendidos en Mercado Libre. Optimiza tus ventas con herramientas, análisis y tips clave para destacar en el marketplace más grande de Latinoamérica.
body_text: Mercado Libre es uno de los marketplaces más populares de Latinoamérica. Saber qué productos son tendencia puede marcar la diferencia en tus estrategias de venta en línea. Aumentar tus ingresos, optimizar inventarios y mejorar tus estrategias de marketing son solo algunos de los beneficios de identificar los productos más demandados. Descubre aquí cómo hacerlo. 1. Utiliza las categorías destacadas de Mercado Libre Mercado Libre clasifica sus productos en diversas categorías y subcategorías. Las más populares suelen aparecer en la página principal del sitio o en los rankings de cada categoría, accesibles desde el menú de navegación principal. Navega por estas listas para identificar qué artículos tienen mayor demanda. Las categorías como electrónica, moda y hogar suelen ser grandes protagonistas. Tip: Busca la etiqueta “Más vendido” o “Tendencia” en los productos. Estas etiquetas son asignadas automáticamente por Mercado Libre a los artículos con mayores ventas. 2. Analiza las búsquedas más populares Mercado Libre cuenta con herramientas internas que muestran las búsquedas más frecuentes realizadas por los usuarios, como las sugerencias de autocompletado. Estas pueden darte una idea clara de lo que las personas están buscando. Además, algunas plataformas de terceros también ofrecen esta información. Herramientas recomendadas: Google Trends: Compara palabras clave relacionadas con productos para ver cuáles son tendencia. SEMrush o Ahrefs: Estas herramientas SEO te permiten analizar el volumen de búsqueda y la competencia de ciertas palabras clave asociadas a Mercado Libre. 3. Revisa los comentarios y calificaciones Los comentarios y calificaciones son un tesoro de información. Productos con una alta cantidad de reseñas positivas y ventas constantes suelen ser los favoritos. Por ejemplo, en la categoría de electrónica, productos como audífonos inalámbricos suelen tener miles de reseñas positivas, lo que indica una demanda constante. Además, los comentarios pueden darte pistas sobre los beneficios o problemas recurrentes de los productos, lo que te ayudará a identificar oportunidades para mejorar tu oferta. Tip: Fíjate en la fecha de las reseñas más recientes. Un producto con muchas ventas en el último mes tiene mayor probabilidad de seguir siendo popular. 4. Observa a tu competencia Identificar qué está vendiendo tu competencia también es una estrategia inteligente. Busca vendedores con buenas calificaciones y revisa sus catálogos. Observa qué productos se repiten y cuáles tienen mejores reseñas y índices de venta. Tip: Utiliza herramientas como Keepsa o Jungle Scout para monitorear tendencias y ventas en marketplaces similares a Mercado Libre. 5. Usa herramientas de análisis de datos Existen herramientas específicas diseñadas para analizar marketplaces. Estas plataformas recopilan información sobre los productos más vendidos, precios promedio y movimientos de mercado. Algunas opciones populares incluyen: Nubimetrics: Una herramienta enfocada en Mercado Libre que te permite identificar tendencias de venta. Helium 10: Aunque es más común para Amazon, también puede ser útil para entender qué productos están funcionando. 6. Identifica temporadas y eventos especiales Las ventas en Mercado Libre también están influenciadas por eventos como el Buen Fin, Navidad o la temporada de regreso a clases. Durante estas fechas, los productos como electrónica, juguetes y útiles escolares suelen liderar las ventas.
